problems.quote: Sachchidanand Hushang Pandey v. Union of India (2015)
problems.problem: Wrong case name for the NJAC judgment; the 99th Amendment was struck down in Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (2015).
problems.correction: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (2015)
problems.verifierReason: The NJAC judgment striking down the 99th Amendment is correctly cited as Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (2015); the quoted name is incorrect.

problems.quote: placing an adjective after the noun in Hindi or Sanskrit-based languages
problems.problem: In Hindi, attributive adjectives standardly precede the noun (e.g., 'अच्छा लड़का' good boy); post-nominal position is for predicative use with a copula, not the default modification structure.
problems.correction: placing an adjective before the noun in Hindi (the standard attributive order)
problems.verifierReason: Hindi attributive adjectives precede nouns; post-nominal is predicative only.

problems.quote: translating a Hindi sentence where the object precedes the verb
problems.problem: In 'Yeh ghar mera hai', 'mera' is a predicate adjective (complement), not an object; the clause is Subject-Complement-Verb, not Subject-Object-Verb.
problems.correction: translating a Hindi sentence where the complement precedes the verb
problems.verifierReason: 'Mera' in 'Yeh ghar mera hai' is a predicate complement, not an object.

problems.quote: culturally equivalent expression like 'Barrage ho raha hai' (A barrage is happening)
problems.problem: 'Barrage ho raha hai' is not a Hindi idiom for heavy rain; common idioms are 'मूसलाधार बारिश हो रही है' (musladhar barish ho rahi hai) or 'झमाझम बारिश' (jhamajham barish).
problems.correction: culturally equivalent expression like 'मूसलाधार बारिश हो रही है' (torrential rain is happening)
problems.verifierReason: 'Barrage ho raha hai' is not a Hindi idiom; 'musladhar barish' is standard.

problems.quote: Data from linguistic studies suggests that up to 30% of translation errors in competitive exams stem from misinterpreting these cultural markers rather than grammar
problems.problem: The precise figure '30%' and the attribution to 'linguistic studies' are unsourced and appear invented for this text.
problems.correction: Some linguistic analyses suggest a significant share of translation errors in competitive exams stem from misinterpreting cultural markers rather than grammar
problems.verifierReason: The '30%' figure is unsourced and likely fabricated; hedged phrasing is appropriate.

problems.quote: 2020 amendment to the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act
problems.problem: The Aadhaar Act was amended in 2019 (Aadhaar and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2019), not 2020.
problems.verifierReason: Aadhaar Act amended in 2019 via Aadhaar and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2019; no 2020 amendment.

problems.quote: Family Labour is a significant advantage as it has zero opportunity cost (it does not have to be paid like hired labour).
problems.problem: Family labour has an opportunity cost (the value of the next best alternative use of their time); it is not zero.
problems.correction: Family Labour is a significant advantage as it has low explicit cost, but it carries an opportunity cost.
problems.verifierReason: Original wrongly claims zero opportunity cost; correction correctly states family labour has opportunity cost.

problems.quote: The most fundamental concept is the Crop Production Index , which measures the yield per unit area (e.g., quintals per hectare).
problems.problem: Crop Production Index measures changes in total production over time, not yield per unit area. Yield per unit area is measured by Crop Yield Index or productivity index.
problems.correction: The most fundamental concept is the Crop Yield Index, which measures the yield per unit area (e.g., quintals per hectare).
problems.verifierReason: Crop Production Index tracks production volume, not yield; correction rightly names Crop Yield Index for yield per area.

problems.quote: The Model APMC Act 2003 and its 2017 amendment introduced provisions for private markets, direct marketing, contract farming, and a single‑point levy
problems.problem: The 2017 model law is a separate legislation (The Agricultural Produce and Livestock Marketing (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2017), not an amendment to the 2003 act.
problems.correction: The Model APMC Act 2003 and the 2017 Model Agricultural Produce and Livestock Marketing Act introduced provisions for private markets, direct marketing, contract farming, and a single‑point levy
problems.verifierReason: 2017 model law is separate legislation, not an amendment; correction accurately lists both distinct acts.

problems.quote: each litre of cool water consumed can dissipate approximately 1.2 MJ
problems.problem: The energy dissipated by heating 1 litre of water from 15–20 °C to body temperature (~38 °C) is about 0.1 MJ, not 1.2 MJ.
problems.correction: each litre of cool water consumed can dissipate approximately 0.1 MJ
problems.verifierReason: Physics: heating 1 L water by ~20 K requires ~0.1 MJ, not 1.2 MJ.

problems.quote: a pooled budget mechanism under the National Health Mission and the National Livestock Mission
problems.problem: No pooled budget mechanism exists under NHM and NLM for One Health; the National One Health Mission has its own separate budget.
problems.correction: a dedicated budget under the National One Health Mission
problems.verifierReason: National One Health Mission (launched 2022) has its own dedicated budget; no pooled NHM-NLM mechanism exists for One Health.
